1. (Currently Amended) A method for controlling a flow of air, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in a booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; and terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value, __wherein the pump is controlled to reduce parasitic load on an engine driving the pump__.

2. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced, __and wherein the directional control valve is actuated based on a signal from a vacuum sensor__.

3. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device, __wherein the directional control valve is a solenoid-operated three-way valve__.

4. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, __wherein the negative pressure chamber is isolated from the booster device__.

5. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere, __wherein the pump outlet is vented to atmosphere through the directional control valve__.

6. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 5, further comprising filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump via a filter, __wherein the filter is a particulate air filter having a minimum efficiency rating of MERV 8 or higher__.

7. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

8. (Currently Amended) A system for controlling a flow of air, the system comprising: a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced, __wherein the directional control valve is controlled by a vacuum sensor that monitors the vacuum level in the booster device__.

9. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, __wherein the directional control valve is a solenoid-operated three-way valve__.

10. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, __wherein the negative pressure chamber is isolated from the booster device__.

11. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere, __wherein the pump outlet is vented to atmosphere through the directional control valve__.

12. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 11, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering a flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump, __wherein the filter is a particulate air filter having a minimum efficiency rating of MERV 8 or higher__.

13. (Original) The system of claim 8, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

14. (Currently Amended) A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump and a parasitic load on the engine are reduced, __wherein the directional control valve is controlled by a vacuum sensor that monitors the vacuum level in the booster device and automatically switches the directional control valve when the predetermined vacuum level is reached__.

15. (Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, __wherein the directional control valve is a solenoid-operated three-way valve__.

16. (Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, __wherein the negative pressure chamber is isolated from the booster device__.

17. (Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere, __wherein the pump outlet is vented to atmosphere through the directional control valve__.

18. (Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 17, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump, __wherein the filter is a particulate air filter having a minimum efficiency rating of MERV 8 or higher__.

19. (Original) The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system.

20. (Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the engine is a compression-ignition type, __and wherein the pump is a variable displacement pump that adjusts displacement based on the vacuum level in the booster device__.
